summary: The non_gaia variant is the most complete implementation of the three: it contains dedicated Python agents for every major requirement and data models for animals, staff, tasks, vaccination schedules, cleaning tasks, adoption processes, and emergencies. The system has stronger component coverage than the GAIA variants, and the Python files compile. It still needs revision because task lifecycle tracking is thin, dependencies are not pinned exactly, and debug/demo output remains embedded in executable paths.

findings.description: The variant defines dedicated agents for all major requirement areas, including admission, adoption, registry, calendar/vaccination, cleaning, emergency handling, priority handling, rotation, staff management, task assignment, and task generation.
findings.evidence: Examples: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/admission_agent.py:9 class AdmissionAgent(Agent); non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/adoption_agent.py:9 class AdoptionAgent(Agent); non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/priority_agent.py:9 class PriorityAgent(Agent); non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/rotation_agent.py:11 class RotationAgent(Agent).

findings.description: Task assignment explicitly attempts to select staff based on the task and available staff list.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/task_assignment_agent.py:23 def assign_task(self, task_id: str, staff_members: List[str] = None) -> 'TaskAssignment'; line 111 def _find_best_staff_member(self, task: 'Task', staff_list: List['StaffMember']) -> 'StaffMember'.

findings.description: The system persists generated tasks and assignments, but there is no clearly named task completion/update-status agent operation matching the requirement to monitor the full task lifecycle and confirm completion by workers.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/task_generation_agent.py:32 status="otwarte"; non_gaia/implementation_workspace/utils/database.py:54 def save_task(self, task: Task); non_gaia/implementation_workspace/utils/database.py:154 def get_task_assignment(self, task_id: str) -> Optional[TaskAssignment].

findings.description: Emergency handling is explicitly modeled with schedule reconfiguration behavior.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/agents/emergency_agent.py:13 goal="Instantly reconfigure schedules in case of emergencies such as new animal admissions or staff unavailability."; line 138 def reconfigure_schedule_for_emergency(self, emergency_type: str, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any].

findings.description: Debug/demo print statements are embedded in executable paths instead of using structured logging or test fixtures.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/animal_shelter_system.py:16 print("Creating animal shelter management system..."); static summary found 43 print calls.

findings.description: Dependencies are specified with lower bounds rather than exact pins, which can reduce reproducibility.
All Python files in the variant compile without syntax errors.

logical_inconsistencies: Task creation and assignment are represented, but lifecycle completion/worker confirmation is less explicit than the rest of the requirement coverage.
implementation_risks: Task status may remain open without a clear worker confirmation workflow.
Lower-bound dependency specifications can introduce breaking changes from future package releases.
Runtime behavior is difficult to validate because the project contains demo output paths but no discovered test suite.
